10:1.sourceText: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ἐν Καισαρίᾳ ὀνόματι Κορνήλιος, ἑκατοντάρχης ἐκ σπείρης τῆς καλουμένης Ἰταλικῆς,
10:1.targetText: And there was a certain man in Caesarea, by name Cornelius, a centurion from a cohort that is called Italian,

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned N1904 introduction is nominal, without a finite be verb. The pinned CrossWire TR prints ἦν, matching this longer English introduction.

10:2.sourceText: εὐσεβὴς καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν Θεὸν σὺν παντὶ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, ποιῶν ἐλεημοσύνας πολλὰς τῷ λαῷ καὶ δεόμενος τοῦ Θεοῦ διὰ παντός,
10:2.targetText: pious, and fearing God with all his house, also doing many kind acts to the people, and always imploring God;

groups.note: The actual plural noun is ἐλεημοσύνας, alms or charitable gifts, rendered kind acts; this is one noun rather than separate Greek words for kind and acts.
The preposition and substantival adjective διὰ παντός form the adverbial expression rendered always.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before God and the possessive house construction have no separate English article.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned N1904 has no connective here; the pinned CrossWire TR has τε beside the doing/alms clause.

10:3.sourceText: εἶδεν ἐν ὁράματι φανερῶς, ὡσεὶ περὶ ὥραν ἐνάτην τῆς ἡμέρας, ἄγγελον τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσελθόντα πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ εἰπόντα αὐτῷ Κορνήλιε.
10:3.targetText: he saw in a vision openly, as it were the ninth hour of the day, a messenger of God coming in to him, and saying to him, “Cornelius”;

groups.note: The paired approximating expressions ὡσεὶ περί qualify the time; the English as it were expresses this approximation, not a separately written be verb.

10:4.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἔμφοβος γενόμενος εἶπεν Τί ἐστιν, Κύριε; εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Αἱ προσευχαί σου καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἀνέβησαν εἰς μνημόσυνον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
10:4.targetText: and he having looked earnestly on him, and becoming afraid, said, “What is it, Lord?” And he said to him, “Your prayers and your kind acts came up for a memorial before God,

groups.note: The actual dative αὐτῷ is the same recipient of the earnest look; English supplies on in expressing that dative complement.
The actual noun names alms or charitable gifts; English kind acts renders that single lexical head.

unmappedSource.reason: These articles are not separately represented in the possessive prayer/alms phrases or before God.

10:5.sourceText: καὶ νῦν πέμψον ἄνδρας εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνά τινα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος·
10:5.targetText: and now send men to Joppa, and send for a certain one Simon, who is surnamed Peter;

10:6.sourceText: οὗτος ξενίζεται παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ, ᾧ ἐστιν οἰκία παρὰ θάλασσαν.
10:6.targetText: this one lodges with a certain Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea; this one will speak to you what you must do.”

groups.note: The relative ᾧ is dative, expressing the person to whom the house belongs. English whose recasts that same dative possessor as a genitive relative.

unmappedTarget.text: this one will speak to you what you must do
unmappedTarget.reason: This entire additional speech clause is absent from pinned N1904 and present in the pinned CrossWire TR. No words from the parallel account are imported as its source.

10:7.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ λαλῶν αὐτῷ, φωνήσας δύο τῶν οἰκετῶν καὶ στρατιώτην εὐσεβῆ τῶν προσκαρτερούντων αὐτῷ,
10:7.targetText: And when the messenger who is speaking to Cornelius went away, having called two of his servants, and a pious soldier of those waiting on him continually,

unmappedSource.reason: The pinned source has αὐτῷ, to him, whereas the pinned CrossWire TR names τῷ Κορνηλίῳ and the English names Cornelius. The differing source expressions remain unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English named recipient follows the pinned TR τῷ Κορνηλίῳ rather than N1904 αὐτῷ, to him.
The pinned TR has an additional αὐτοῦ with the servants; that possessive is absent from pinned N1904. The later on him is a different written pronoun.

10:8.sourceText: καὶ ἐξηγησάμενος ἅπαντα αὐτοῖς ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Ἰόππην.
10:8.targetText: and having expounded all things to them, he sent them to Joppa.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Joppa is not separately expressed in English.

10:9.sourceText: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ὁδοιπορούντων ἐκείνων καὶ τῇ πόλει ἐγγιζόντων ἀνέβη Πέτρος ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα προσεύξασθαι περὶ ὥραν ἕκτην.
10:9.targetText: And on the next day, as these are proceeding on the way, and are drawing near to the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour,

groups.note: The genitive participle ὁδοιπορούντων is a single traveling verb, expanded as are proceeding on the way; English as expresses the circumstantial construction.
The actual genitive demonstrative is the personal subject of the genitive-absolute traveling clause, recast as English these.

10:10.sourceText: ἐγένετο δὲ πρόσπεινος καὶ ἤθελεν γεύσασθαι· παρασκευαζόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐγένετο ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔκστασις,
10:10.targetText: and he became very hungry, and wished to eat; and they making ready, there fell on him a trance,

groups.note: The actual middle infinitive γεύσασθαι is from γεύομαι, taste or eat; English to eat renders that verb, not a separately written ἐσθίω.
The genitive αὐτῶν is the personal subject of the preparing genitive absolute, rendered nominative they.

unmappedSource.reason: The pinned N1904 predicate is ἐγένετο, happened or came about. The pinned TR instead prints ἐπέπεσεν, fell upon, behind the English there fell; the differing predicates remain explicit source gaps.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has the falling predicate ἐπέπεσεν; pinned N1904 has ἐγένετο, happened, rather than that lexical head.

10:11.sourceText: καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγμένον καὶ καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην, τέσσαρσιν ἀρχαῖς καθιέμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς,
10:11.targetText: and he beholds Heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending to him, as a great sheet, bound at the four corners, and let down on the earth,

groups.note: The dative numeral and corners noun express the four lowering points. English at the four corners supplies the case relation; its attachment to the extra bound wording follows the longer TR construction, not an additional N1904 binding predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Heaven is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν after descending; pinned N1904 has no corresponding recipient phrase here.
The pinned TR has δεδεμένον, bound, which is absent from pinned N1904.
The pinned TR has an additional coordinator before let down, absent from pinned N1904.

10:12.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ ὑπῆρχεν πάντα τὰ τετράποδα καὶ ἑρπετὰ τῆς γῆς καὶ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
10:12.targetText: in which were all the four-footed beasts of the earth, and the wild beasts, and the creeping things, and the birds of the sky,

groups.note: The actual τετράποδα is a substantival adjective, four-footed ones; English beasts makes the implied animal head explicit without a separate Greek θηρία here.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR includes καὶ τὰ θηρία, and the wild beasts, absent from pinned N1904.

10:13.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ πρὸς αὐτόν Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε.
10:13.targetText: and there came a voice to him: “Having risen, Peter, slay and eat.”

10:14.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος εἶπεν Μηδαμῶς, Κύριε, ὅτι οὐδέποτε ἔφαγον πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ἀκάθαρτον.
10:14.targetText: And Peter said, “Not so, Lord; because at no time did I eat anything common or unclean”;

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Peter is not separately expressed.
The pinned N1904 has καί, and, whereas the pinned TR has ἤ, or, as in the English list.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR reads ἤ where N1904 reads καί; the differing coordinators are not conflated.

10:15.sourceText: καὶ φωνὴ πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου πρὸς αὐτόν Ἃ ὁ Θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου.
10:15.targetText: and [there is] a voice again a second time to him: “What God cleansed, you do not declare common”;

groups.note: The actual present imperative κοινοῦ is a single making-or-regarding-common verb. English do declare common expands that predicate, not a separate Greek declaring verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The Greek introduction names a voice without a written finite be verb; English supplies the bracketed copula.

10:16.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς, καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνελήμφθη τὸ σκεῦος εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
10:16.targetText: and this was done three times, and again was the vessel received up to Heaven.

groups.note: The actual ἐγένετο is a middle-form happened/came-about predicate, rendered was done; it is not a printed passive form of ποιέω.

unmappedSource.reason: The pinned N1904 reads εὐθύς, immediately, while the pinned TR reads πάλιν, again, followed by the English.
The article before Heaven is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows TR πάλιν rather than N1904 εὐθύς, immediately.

10:17.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ διηπόρει ὁ Πέτρος τί ἂν εἴη τὸ ὅραμα ὃ εἶδεν, ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Κορνηλίου διερωτήσαντες τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ Σίμωνος ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὸν πυλῶνα,
10:17.targetText: And as Peter was perplexed in himself what the vision that he saw might be, then, behold, the men who have been sent from Cornelius, having made inquiry for the house of Simon, stood at the gate,

groups.note: The modal particle ἄν with optative εἴη forms the potential clause rendered might be; the source analysis is optative, not future or subjunctive.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before the personal names are not separately expressed in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: This English connective has no separately written τότε or equivalent after the vision clause in pinned N1904.

10:18.sourceText: καὶ φωνήσαντες ἐπυνθάνοντο εἰ Σίμων ὁ ἐπικαλούμενος Πέτρος ἐνθάδε ξενίζεται.
10:18.targetText: and having called, they were asking if Simon, who is surnamed Peter, lodges here.

groups.note: The actual ξενίζεται is passive in the pinned analysis, being hosted or lodged; English lodges is an intransitive rendering of that same lodging predicate.

10:19.sourceText: Τοῦ δὲ Πέτρου διενθυμουμένου περὶ τοῦ ὁράματος εἶπεν τὸ Πνεῦμα Ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ζητοῦντές σε·
10:19.targetText: And Peter thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men seek you;

groups.note: The actual seeking word is a present participle, rendered as the English finite seek in this announcement; no separate finite seeking verb is introduced.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Peter in the genitive absolute is not separately represented.
The pinned N1904 reads δύο, two, while the pinned TR reads τρεῖς, three. The differing numerals are unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR numeral τρεῖς rather than the N1904 δύο.
The pinned TR supplies αὐτῷ with the Spirit said clause; that recipient pronoun is absent from pinned N1904.

10:20.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἀναστὰς κατάβηθι, καὶ πορεύου σὺν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀπέσταλκα αὐτούς.
10:20.targetText: but having risen, go down and go on with them, doubting nothing, because I have sent them”;

10:21.sourceText: καταβὰς δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς τοὺς ἄνδρας εἶπεν Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ εἰμι ὃν ζητεῖτε· τίς ἡ αἰτία δι’ ἣν πάρεστε;
10:21.targetText: and Peter having come down to the men who have been sent from Cornelius to him, said, “Behold, I am he whom you seek, what [is] the cause for which you are present?”

unmappedTarget.reason: This qualifying relative/sending/recipient clause is absent from pinned N1904 and present in the pinned TR.

10:22.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Κορνήλιος ἑκατοντάρχης, ἀνὴρ δίκαιος καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν Θεὸν, μαρτυρούμενός τε ὑπὸ ὅλου τοῦ ἔθνους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐχρηματίσθη ὑπὸ ἀγγέλου ἁγίου μεταπέμψασθαί σε εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ῥήματα παρὰ σοῦ.
10:22.targetText: And they said, “Cornelius, a centurion, a man righteous and fearing God, well testified to, also, by all the nation of the Jews, was divinely warned by a holy messenger to send for you, to his house, and to hear sayings from you.”

The actual passive χρηματίζω has the lexical sense of receiving divine instruction or warning, hence was divinely warned; no separate God noun is inserted. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/chrematizo .

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before God and the possessive house phrase are not separately expressed.

10:23.sourceText: εἰσκαλεσάμενος οὖν αὐτοὺς ἐξένισεν. Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς, καί τινες τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἀπὸ Ἰόππης συνῆλθον αὐτῷ.
10:23.targetText: Having called them in, therefore, he lodged them, and on the next day Peter went forth with them, and certain of the brothers from Joppa went with him,

groups.note: The one actual αὐτούς is the same men called in and lodged; English repeats them for the two immediate coordinated actions.

The repeated article introducing the from Joppa modifier has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR explicitly names Peter here; N1904 instead has the rising participle and an understood subject.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Peter, Cornelius, and the contextually possessed feet are not separately expressed in English.

10:29.sourceText: διὸ καὶ ἀναντιρρήτως ἦλθον μεταπεμφθείς. πυνθάνομαι οὖν Τίνι λόγῳ μετεπέμψασθέ με.

10:30.sourceText: Καὶ ὁ Κορνήλιος ἔφη Ἀπὸ τετάρτης ἡμέρας μέχρι ταύτης τῆς ὥρας ἤμην τὴν ἐνάτην προσευχόμενος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἔστη ἐνώπιόν μου ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ,

10:38.sourceText: Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ, ὡς ἔχρισεν αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ καὶ δυνάμει, ὃς διῆλθεν εὐεργετῶν καὶ ἰώμενος πάντας τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἦν μετ’ αὐτοῦ·
10:38.targetText: Jesus who [is] from Nazareth—how God anointed Him with the Holy Spirit and power; who went through, doing good, and healing all those oppressed by the Devil, because God was with Him;

groups.note: The dative Spirit phrase expresses the instrument or means, rendered with the Holy Spirit; no separately written with preposition is introduced.
The actual εὐεργετῶν is a single doing-good verb, rendered doing good rather than two separate Greek lexical heads.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before God are not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The attributive from Nazareth construction contains no written be verb; English supplies bracketed is.

10:39.sourceText: καὶ ἡμεῖς μάρτυρες πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἔν τε τῇ χώρᾳ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ Ἱερουσαλήμ· ὃν καὶ ἀνεῖλαν κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου.
10:39.targetText: and we are witnesses of all things that He did, both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem—whom they slew, having hanged [Him] on a tree.

groups.note: The one actual ἐν governs the coordinated country and Jerusalem locations; English repeats in before the second location.

The actual relative ὃν supplies the same person as patient of both the killing and immediate hanging predicate; English resumes that patient with bracketed Him. One written relative is retained, not an invented additional pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual additional καί beside the killing clause is not separately expressed in this English sentence.

unmappedTarget.reason: N1904 has a nominal we witnesses clause without a written be verb; the pinned TR includes ἐσμέν, are.

10:40.sourceText: τοῦτον ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν ἐμφανῆ γενέσθαι,
10:40.targetText: This One God raised up [on] the third day, and gave Him to become visible,

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God is not separately expressed.

10:41.sourceText: οὐ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ, ἀλλὰ μάρτυσιν τοῖς προκεχειροτονημένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἡμῖν, οἵτινες συνεφάγομεν καὶ συνεπίομεν αὐτῷ μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
10:41.targetText: not to all the people, but to witnesses, to those having been chosen before by God—to us who ate with [Him], and drank with Him, after His rising out of the dead;

groups.note: The actual dative αὐτῷ names the companion for the coordinated eating-with and drinking-with predicates. English repeats Him with these immediate parallel actions; there is one written companion pronoun.
The actual accusative αὐτόν is the personal subject of the rising infinitive; English expresses that same person as the possessive His modifying rising.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God and the articular infinitive under the English possessive rising expression are not separately expressed.

10:42.sourceText: καὶ παρήγγειλεν ἡμῖν κηρύξαι τῷ λαῷ καὶ διαμαρτύρασθαι ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ὡρισμένος ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ Κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν.
10:42.targetText: and He commanded us to preach to the people, and to fully testify that it is He who has been ordained judge of living and dead by God—

groups.note: The actual finite ἐστιν supplies the English it is construction, while the adjacent actual demonstrative οὗτος owns He; the introductory it is the English clause recast, not a second Greek personal pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God is not separately expressed.

10:43.sourceText: τούτῳ πάντες οἱ προφῆται μαρτυροῦσιν, ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβεῖν διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτόν.
10:43.targetText: to this One do all the Prophets testify, that through His Name everyone that is believing in Him receives forgiveness of sins.”

groups.note: The actual λαβεῖν is an aorist active infinitive, rendered as finite receives in the English content clause. No source present indicative form is substituted.

unmappedSource.reason: The genitive article before the possessive His Name is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: This English introduces the content of testimony; the Greek has an infinitival receiving clause rather than a separately written ὅτι.

10:44.sourceText: Ἔτι λαλοῦντος τοῦ Πέτρου τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐπέπεσεν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας τὸν λόγον.
10:44.targetText: While Peter is yet speaking these sayings, the Holy Spirit fell on all those hearing the word,

groups.note: The genitive-absolute speaking participle is rendered by the English circumstantial While ... is ... speaking clause; is belongs to the real verbal predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Peter, the article in these sayings, and the repeated article before Holy are not separately expressed in English.

10:45.sourceText: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς πιστοὶ ὅσοι συνῆλθαν τῷ Πέτρῳ, ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἡ δωρεὰ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος ἐκκέχυται·
10:45.targetText: and those of circumcision [who were] believing were astonished—as many as came with Peter—because the gift of the Holy Spirit has also been poured out on the nations,

groups.note: The actual πιστοί is a nominative plural adjective, believing or faithful, used for persons. The bracketed who were is separately recorded as English expansion.

unmappedSource.reason: The dative article before Peter has no separate English article; with is expressed by the actual accompanying verb συνῆλθαν.

unmappedTarget.reason: The actual πιστοί is a believing/faithful adjective, not a verbal participle or be verb. English supplies the bracketed relative copula.

10:46.sourceText: ἤκουον γὰρ αὐτῶν λαλούντων γλώσσαις καὶ μεγαλυνόντων τὸν Θεόν. τότε ἀπεκρίθη Πέτρος
10:46.targetText: for they were hearing them speaking with tongues and magnifying God.

groups.note: The actual genitive αὐτῶν is the personal complement of hearing with the speaking/magnifying participles, recast as English accusative them.
The actual dative plural γλώσσαις is rendered with tongues; with expresses the case-governed means rather than a separately written Greek preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God is not separately expressed.

sourceMoved.reason: The actual τότε ἀπεκρίθη Πέτρος closing Greek 10:46 is displayed as Then Peter answered at the beginning of LSV 10:47.

10:47.sourceText: Μήτι τὸ ὕδωρ δύναται κωλῦσαί τις τοῦ μὴ βαπτισθῆναι τούτους, οἵτινες τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἔλαβον ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς;
10:47.targetText: Then Peter answered, “Is anyone able to forbid the water, that these may not be immersed, who received the Holy Spirit—even as us also?”

groups.note: The actual interrogative particle μήτι and finite δύναται jointly form the ability question; the particle contributes its question force without a separately inserted English not.

The article and passive infinitive form the articular-infinitive complement of preventing, expressed as English that these may not be immersed; may is part of this English clause recast, not a second Greek modal verb.
The actual ἡμεῖς is nominative we; English uses us after the comparison, retaining the same first-person plural identity.

unmappedSource.reason: The second article before Holy is not separately expressed.

10:48.sourceText: προσέταξεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ βαπτισθῆναι. τότε ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας τινάς.
10:48.targetText: He commanded them to also be immersed in the Name of the LORD; then they implored him to remain certain days.

unmappedSource.reason: The source connective δέ is not separately expressed as an independent English coordinator.
The pinned N1904 explicitly names Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, Jesus Christ; the pinned TR instead reads τοῦ κυρίου, of the Lord, as in the English. These different named expressions remain whole witness gaps.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR τοῦ κυρίου rather than N1904 Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
The English additive also has no corresponding additive word in this N1904 infinitive clause; the pinned TR has a different connective τε beside the commanded/them wording.
